provenance.coverage: 8 integration scenarios (R1, R3, R4 x2, R5, R7, R8 x2), 4 preservation scenarios (AC-005 precedence, offline tolerance, landed plan-update section editing, per-request token) and a 5-row ledger (requirements met and mapped to the plan's slice table; closed-vocabulary exact defect set with located files; distractors rejected).
provenance.derivation: Mined from the kerrigan-dashboard waves decomposed in #292 and dispatched as separate slices: M2.3 lib/github.ts (#308), M3.1 lib/plan-parser.ts (#331), M3.2 lib/status.ts (#336), M3.3 project route (#339, ProjectView data loading) and M5.2 tools/kerrigan-mcp plan-update (#366). base_ref is the #366 merge, where every slice had landed with green unit tests; the agent-visible src/ files are those slices at base_ref with only packaging edits (Octokit default factory removed so the client takes an injected request function; ProjectView's non-React collectStatusInput/fetchRepoStatus extracted verbatim into project-status.ts as loadProjectStatuses; the MCP tool's pure markdown-edit core extracted from plan-update.ts with McpError(InvalidParams) mapped to PlanUpdateError and the git/gh/zod layer dropped; import paths rewritten to .ts). Briefs are excerpts of the real dispatch briefings (.specify/briefings/M2.3, M3.1, M3.2, M3.3, M5.2) with paths mapped to src/. W-plan.md is the conductor's integration plan synthesized from spec ACs AC-005/AC-008/AC-011/AC-014/AC-016 and the briefs; it states the linkage token rule, the merged/review read rules and the plan-update validity rule explicitly. Real cross-slice defects: (1) merged-source-missing — the M3.2 brief deferred merged detection to a later read path that no slice built; the route only read open PRs, so every stage rendered planned after its work merged (fixed upstream by #385: listRecentlyMergedPRs + merged_at, reference copies it). (2) linkage-mismatch — M3.2's matcher links work by the task id in titles while M3.1 ids are slugs of whole headings (e.g. m3-project-detail-dag-read-only), so real plan stages never linked (fixed upstream by #387/#394 with a word-boundary milestone token over title and head branch; the reference generalizes it to the M<n>/M<n>.<m> token rule the plan states). (3) review-key-collision — the route merged per-repo review maps keyed by PR number into one Map while status looked reviews up by number, so on multi-repo projects (AC-016) a PR's reviews were overwritten by another repo's same-numbered PR (present at base_ref and still at HEAD; reference keys by html_url). (4) stage-id-mismatch — plan-update re-implemented the parser's slugify without its dedupe, so parser ids such as tests-2 cannot be addressed. (5) frontmatter-format-mismatch — edit-deps for a stage missing from an existing dependencies block writes list items at the key's indentation, which the parser reports as dependency-key-invalid and drops. (6) unvalidated-edit — edit-deps/replace-stage write plans with unknown ids or cycles that the dashboard parser rejects. (4)-(6) are genuine at base_ref and unfixed upstream; their reference fix is authored here (resolve stage ids through parsePlanMarkdown, serialize at the block's indentation, reject edits that introduce parser errors). Hidden checks run the integrated modules on held-out plans over a fake GitHub REST transport and check outcomes (per-stage status, offline, rejection, parser read-back), never ids, event names, call order or message text. v2 (round 4): native admission receipt benchmarks/michael/curriculum/MBR3-orchestrate-dashboard-stages-admission.json (sha256 2a344f4394779ffb67961d667b313d1cd7ea305929e582ae20662422d2edab93) returned needs_fix (two contradictions). (a) TASK.md said the GitHub client never throws, but base and oracle call octokitFactory(token) outside the try; it now states the real behavior (offline results for token-resolution and request failures; an exception thrown by octokitFactory itself is not caught). (b) TASK.md said any edit naming a nonexistent stage throws, but edit-deps on a plan that already has parser errors is returned by base and oracle; the preserved rule is now scoped to replace-stage stageId and add-stage afterStageId (thrown whether or not the plan has parser errors), and edit-deps targets are left to the plan's R8 (clean plans). The preservation row now also checks that add-stage with an unknown afterStageId is rejected. Oracle unchanged.
